questions.q: Why must Lesson 9's custom objects (Installation Project, Service Contract) be built before Lesson 11's sharing rules?
options: Sharing rules in Chapter 3 are written against those real objects, so they must exist before the rules can reference them
Salesforce requires custom objects to be created in a fixed order by creation date
Custom objects automatically generate their own sharing rules when created
Sharing rules can only be written against standard objects, not custom ones
questions.explain: The lesson states the data model must exist before security can be implemented against it -- sharing rules in Chapter 3 reference Installation Project and Service Contract directly, so those objects must already exist.

questions.q: Which chapter in this capstone is described as "purely additive," and what does that mean for build order?
options: Chapter 1, because it only contains planning lessons
Chapter 3, because Flows add new fields automatically
Chapter 2, because every lesson in it creates a brand-new object
Chapter 4, because it never changes the object model -- it only uses what already exists
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly calls Chapter 4 purely additive: its reports, dashboard, and sample data use the object model and automation already built, without changing it.

questions.q: Per the build sequence, what must be true before Chapter 3's Flows and validation rules (Lessons 12-13) are built?
options: Lesson 11's security model must already be implemented, so automation is never built against an unfinished security design
Chapter 4's reports must already exist
The approval process in Lesson 14 must be built first
Nothing -- Lessons 12-13 have no dependencies
questions.explain: The lesson states Chapter 3's automation lessons all wait on Lesson 11 so that Flows and validation rules never get built against a security model that isn't finished yet.

questions.q: What three concrete artifacts does this lesson say you need before moving from Chapter 1 into Chapter 2?
options: A signed contract, a budget approval, and a project charter
The Lesson 3 data model diagram, the Lesson 4 security model, and this lesson's build sequence
A completed Trailhead badge, a certification exam date, and a resume draft
A list of competitor CRM products and their pricing
questions.explain: The lesson lists exactly these three: the data model diagram from Lesson 3, the security model from Lesson 4, and the build sequence from this lesson, pinned somewhere to keep checking.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what kind of problem does planning the build order in advance prevent?
options: Slow page-load times in the finished org
Rework -- redoing already-built configuration because something it depended on wasn't finished yet
Running out of available object names in Salesforce
Exceeding the number of custom fields allowed per org
questions.explain: The lesson's central argument is that getting build order wrong creates real rework -- for example, you can't set sharing rules on an object that doesn't exist yet -- which is exactly what this lesson's sequence is designed to prevent.
